taxonomic_note: Kew/POWO accepted name used canonically. Some regional sources show an expanded author citation; the taxon concept is the same.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: typically ONE to THREE curved combs or 'eyebrows' clustered at the TOP of the flowering stem, with many closely packed spikelets all the way to the raceme tip. Blue grama normally does NOT leave a long naked pointed tip beyond the final spikelet; compare with hairy grama's stinger.
project_tracker_diagnostic: perennial tufted/caespitose warm-season grass with short stout rhizomes; leaves concentrated mainly near the base; usually 1–3 conspicuous curved unilateral pectinate racemes; racemes about 1.5–5 cm long and spreading to arcuate; many crowded spikelets continue to the end of the raceme; no long naked rachis tip or 'stinger' beyond the spikelets

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Beautiful Hays County documents volunteer Bouteloua gracilis thriving on an unmanaged dry slope and treats it within the local native-grass context; BONAP is retained as the primary native-range authority. Uvalde — Texas A&M/OakTrust Uvalde vascular-plant survey records Bouteloua gracilis collected in Uvalde (collection 824, 25 Oct 2002). Crockett — USDA-NRCS Plant Materials Center blue grama evaluation lists accession 9093104 with origin Crockett County, Texas.

crew_field_steps: Count the conspicuous curved eyebrows on ONE flowering stem, avoiding nearby stems behind the subject.
Follow an individual comb from stem attachment along its packed spikelets to the end; look for a naked extended rachis tip or lack thereof.
Against hairy grama's bristly branch with exposed projecting tip and Texas grama's numerous short fuzzy heads, use close seedhead architecture; not purple color.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Complete erect flowering stem with count of terminal branches and visible base.
Same-scale exact-blue comb showing tip, spikelet arrangement, and whether rachis extends bare.
Flowering details with anthers (not confused with spikelets).
Leaf sheath/ligule; compare with B. hirsuta and B. rigidiseta.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Blue grama usually bears 1–3 long curved terminal eyebrow combs whose spikelets extend nearly to the end. Hairy grama often has dense long hairs and a conspicuously bare terminal rachis projection. Pectinata is generally taller with longer and often more numerous combs but overlaps hairy. Texas grama has several much shorter bristly clustered branches. Sideoats has many short side branches all the way down a long stem.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Blue grama: real pollen anthers → curved comb → collar → rooted tuft
steps: PUBLIC PHOTO FIRST: Patrick Alexander's CC0 original photographs mature long, one-sided curved eyebrow-shaped flowering branches and their fine awnlike projections. It is actual blue grama, not a generic grass or a different species.

SECOND: Matt Lavin's archived real species-labelled photo documents hairy blade/sheath and collar REGION, but the exact free inner ligule edge and mm scale cannot yet be verified. Do not relabel the visible sheath hairs as the true ligule.
OTHER PUBLIC PHOTOS show the low bunched habit and an actual detached mature comb; those identify the gross posture but do not explain precise glume and lemma insertions.
Compare to hairy grama Bouteloua hirsuta: both have combs; to distinguish them examine genuine comb rachis tip and actual swollen-base hair placement, not just head curvature alone.

MISSING ABOVEGROUND MACRO: fully open the true inner blade/sheath junction and photograph the fringe ligule separately with 1-mm reference; isolate actual mature branch spikelets and awn origin with a millimeter scale.
LATER ROOT PHOTO: a connected fibrous rooted crown from a source-verified living bunch; no leaf-stem picture can certify root structure.
PUBLIC DISPLAY RIGHTS: three old CC BY-NC photos are intentionally held from public Learner pending explicitly transferable permission, not deleted from archive.

REAL ROOTS, BUT PRESERVED: Smithsonian's 2016 US 03476248 blue grama herbarium sheet has actual fibrous roots physically connected to a pressed tuft and flowering shoots. This earns HALF-ROLE root evidence, not a living soil root observation. Compare with your own living plant excavation when possible.

TRUE FLOWERING ANATOMY: Matt Lavin's archived 2015 Montana B. gracilis photo directly photographs yellow-green dangling pollen anthers on the actual blue grama eyelash comb. These are real flowers; unlike stiff awns, anthers hang as longer, often yellow-green pollen organs.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — EYEBROWS, THEN BRANCH TIP
field_id_short_tiles.short: Count 1–3(4) curved, one-sided combs on ONE flowering culm, each about 1.5–5 cm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace an undamaged mature comb to its far tip: blue grama's rachis ends in one or more rudimentary spikelets, NOT a conspicuous 5–20 mm naked sharp projection as in hairy grama. Count combs on one connected stem, not several overlapping stems. Existing photos show curved combs but do not prove a calibrated tip character.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL COMB SILHOUETTE — MEASURED ATTACHED TIP STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · PERENNIAL CROWN AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Short-rhizomatous or densely tufted perennial; true ligule is a hair fringe generally <0.5–1 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow basal shoots to a single root crown. Short stout rhizomes can occur, but a low matlike stand photograph is NOT evidence of connected rhizomes or rooting stolons. Open the INNER blade–sheath junction to find the actual short ligule ring/fringe of hairs; separate it from longer lateral collar hairs. SDSU gives <0.5 mm; Utah flora describes the entire ring <1 mm. No archived image resolves the calibrated inner ligule.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COMB AND SPIKELET MEASUREMENTS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Crowded one-sided combs ~1.5–5 cm; mature spikelet bodies usually ~5–6 mm, excluding awns.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase gives 1–3(4) arcuate branches 1.5–5 cm long and 5–6 mm laterally compressed spikelets. Count crowded spikelets along one intact branch; the literature often reports roughly 30–90 per branch, but no archived overview permits a precise count. Pale dangling anthers are NOT glumes, lemmas or awns. Photograph an attached mature comb beside a ruler.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MEASUREMENTS — EXISTING IMAGES NOT CALIBRATED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · TWO GLUMES, FERTILE LEMMA AND ITS AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume ~1.5–3.5 mm; upper ~3.5–6 mm; fertile lemma ~4–6 mm with 3 short awns.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Separate the persistent one-veined LOWER and UPPER glumes before measuring. Kew's GrassBase lower glume is narrower (~3–3.5 mm), while Go Botany includes ~1.5–3.5 mm; Kew upper glume ~5–6 mm and Go Botany ~3.5–6 mm. The basal fertile lemma is three-veined, ~4–6 mm in GrassBase, with central awn ~1–3 mm and shorter lateral awns ~0.5–2 mm. These are literature ranges, not measured from photos. Never assign a floret's awn to the branch rachis.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · STERILE FLORET AND CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Above the fertile floret, find 1(–2) reduced sterile florets; contrast hairy grama's naked branch-tip stinger.
field_id_short_tiles.details: GrassBase describes a reduced apical sterile floret with three awns ~2–3 mm; a Utah flora treatment describes sterile awns ~2.5–5 mm. Dissect the reduced floret separately from the fertile lemma before placing awn arrows. Hairy grama (B. hirsuta) often has spreading hairs and a bare distal rachis; B. pectinata is generally taller with longer/more combs, but overlaps; Texas grama (B. rigidiseta) has several very short bristly units; sideoats grama (B. curtipendula) bears many branches down an extended axis. Reddish/purple color is not decisive.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL DIFFERENT-SPECIES COMPARISON — MATCHED SCALE NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / TWO HANDOFFS
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: six historical image records, five physically archived JPGs and one remote-only seed reference; critical macro and rights/site checks remain.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish): source-authenticated Central Texas connected rooted crown with flowering culm and 1–3(4) combs; exposed 0.5–1 mm hair-fringe ligule with 1-mm scale; undamaged terminal comb tip showing whether last unit is rudimentary spikelet or naked rachis; intact ~5–6 mm spikelet and separated two glumes, fertile lemma with central/lateral awn origins, reduced sterile floret with its own three awns; same-scale B. hirsuta and B. pectinata comparison. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Public Learner Readiness): verify five physically archived JPEGs and the remote-only public-domain seed reference separately; individual CC BY-SA 2.0, CC BY-NC and US federal public-domain provenance; Joey photo-level CC BY-NC version and noncommercial display conditions; four preexisting gross-organ arrows, six historical teaching panels, different-species label, EXIF/GPS handling and phone/mobile overlay. Do not add speculative arrows or mark FINISHED until botanical identity, rights and pixel targets are verified.
